text.headline: Copper leads retreat in industrial metals
text.tone: A sharp decline in copper prices is consistent with confirmed trade tensions, though broader market moves remained relatively quiet during Wednesday's session.
lead: Copper fell 3.6% to $12,750/t on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]], marking the most significant move in a session otherwise characterized by limited volatility. While industrial metals faced pressure, other commodities showed mixed results as platinum gained 1.0%. The VIX volatility index rose 11.1% in the latest data from November 17.

The decline in copper is consistent with confirmed themes regarding US–China trade and tariffs. As a key industrial material, copper often reflects shifts in expectations for global growth and supply chain stability. Headlines indicate ongoing friction over electric vehicle tariffs and the potential ending of China's trade status. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] notes that world stocks remain below their 200-day average.

Currency markets showed the dollar strengthening slightly, with EUR/USD falling 0.2%. This modest dollar strength may have contributed to the 0.4% decline in gold. US Treasury yields were lower in the latest data, with the 10-year yield at 5.10%.

Market participants will monitor whether copper stabilizes or continues its descent. A sustained drop would strengthen the interpretation that trade barriers are impacting industrial demand. The [[markets|Financial Markets]] page tracks these shifts in the context of the current risk-off regime.

briefs.markets: The VIX volatility index rose 11.1% in the latest data, while US large caps fell 0.2% on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page.
briefs.energy: Brent crude rose 0.04% to $92.94 in the latest data, as markets monitor supply risks on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 1.6% to $63,823 on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page, struggling to hold levels amid reports of significant ETF outflows.
briefs.metals: Copper dropped 3.6% to $12,750/t, leading a divergent session for the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]] where platinum managed a 1.0% gain.
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows China and Saudi Arabia among the weakest markets, with yearly price declines of 6.3% and 3.6% respectively.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top-scoring company during a period of relatively calm credit spreads.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] highlights a risk-off regime for Q4 2026, with semiconductors and artificial intelligence themes seeing significant quarterly declines.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell 0.01% on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page, maintaining a 10.4% year-to-date return.
